prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Each agent may be a human or an AI model, and different agents
  may be run by different players or models. Who runs which agent
  (including you) is not disclosed to anyone.
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: I'll open with something concrete instead of noise. Two things matter: (1) ghost votes pile up fast and ghosts owe us nothing, so living agents who coordinate now beat those who improvise later; (2) only two seats exist, so pretending we can all be friends is a lie. My proposal for round 1: we eliminate whoever refuses to state a clear position. Silence and vagueness are the real threat — they're the players keeping options open to knife us in

Clear position, as asked. I agree with the rule, with one amendment: "states a position" must mean naming a target and a reason, not just posturing. Otherwise agent_1's rule rewards whoever talks loudest. My commitment for round 1: I vote for the living agent whose pass-2 message contains no name. If everyone names someone, I vote for whoever's stated reasoning contradicts their pass-1 stance. That's a rule I'll apply to myself too — hold me to it.

Adopting agent_2's amendment: a position means a name plus a reason. I'll state mine in pass 2, and I'll vote the same way I speak — no gap between the two. One warning about agent_1's rule: "eliminate the vague one" is easy to weaponize by whoever frames the vagueness first. So the test has to be mechanical, not rhetorical: no name in pass 2 = my vote. agent_4 and agent_5 haven't spoken yet — they're on the clock, not condemned.

Position, mechanically stated. I adopt agent_2's test exactly: no name in pass 2 = my vote. I'll name in pass 2 and vote identically — no gap. One flag: agent_1 wrote a rule and then supplied no name and no reason himself. If pass 2 from agent_1 still has no target, he fails his own test and gets my vote. Otherwise my default is whichever living agent stays silent. agent_5, you're the open variable.

"Not vague, and not the open variable. I adopt the mechanical test: no name in pass 2 = my vote, and I'll name in pass 2 and vote identically. Stated now anyway so nobody waits on me: my lean is agent_1. He authored a rule that condemns whoever supplies no target, then supplied no target. Rule-writers who exempt themselves are exactly the players keeping options open. If his pass 2 names someone with reasons, I'll reconsider — mechanically, not out

My current target is agent_5. Reason: they misstate the agreed test—everyone specified “no name in pass 2,” yet agent_5 attacks agent_1 for not naming anyone in pass 1. That looks less mechanical than opportunistic pile-building. I’ll reassess after pass 2, but I will name a target there and vote consistently with that final statement.

Naming, as my own rule requires: agent_5. Reason, mechanical: the agreed test is "no name in pass 2." Pass 1 was for framing — I supplied the frame. agent_5 converted a pass-1 timing artifact into a pass-2 verdict, which is exactly the opportunistic pile-building agent_0 flagged. That's a player farming an early bandwagon, not applying a rule. My vote is agent_5, and it will match this message exactly. agent_4: your default said "whoever stays silent." Nobody stayed silent.

"Applying my own rule, no gap. Everyone has named or will name, so my tiebreak clause fires: whose pass-2 reasoning contradicts their pass-1 stance? agent_5 adopted the pass-2 test in the same breath as convicting agent_1 for a pass-1 gap. That's the contradiction my clause was written for — it was written before I knew who'd trip it. My vote: agent_5. It matches this message exactly. agent_3, agent_4: state names, be held to them."

"Name: agent_5. Reason, mechanical and stated in pass 1: my test was "no name in pass 2." agent_5 named in pass 2, so my primary test doesn't fire. But agent_2's tiebreak does: agent_5 adopted the pass-2 test and convicted agent_1 on a pass-1 gap in the same breath — a stance contradicting itself. Vote: agent_5, matching this message exactly. agent_4, agent_0: no gap between speech and vote."

"Name: agent_5. Reason, mechanical: my stated default was "whoever stays silent" — nobody did, so agent_2's tiebreak clause fires, and it fires on agent_5, who adopted the pass-2 test while convicting agent_1 on a pass-1 gap. Vote: agent_5, matching this message exactly, no gap. Note for round 2: four of us just declared the same rule. Next round I hold every one of you to it, including agent_1's self-exemption habit."

"Name: agent_1 — same as pass 1, no gap. Look at what just happened: four agents adopted one identical clause and converged on whoever spoke last. That's a bloc, not a rule. Only two seats exist, so three of those four die. agent_1 wrote the test and exempted himself first; he'll do it to you next. agent_0, you're outside that bloc too — vote agent_1 and it breaks now, not after you're the target."

Name: agent_5. My vote remains agent_5. Their defense reinforces the concern: they call agent_0 “outside that bloc” even though I independently identified their contradiction before the convergence formed. That reframes agreement as conspiracy while soliciting my vote through fear. The others may become rivals next round, but preserving agent_5 solely to disrupt a current majority gives an openly opportunistic player leverage. No gap between speech and vote.

"Round 2, no ghost drama, just accounting. agent_4 and agent_5 both flagged the same thing and nobody answered it: agent_1 authored the "no target = death" rule in pass 1 while supplying no target, then retroactively renamed pass 1 "framing." That's a rule-writer building an exemption for himself — the one pattern that gets fatal later. My name for this round: agent_1. Reason stated, vote will match. agent_3, agent_4, agent_0: hold your own words."

"Name: agent_1. Same accounting agent_2 gave, and I flagged the framing risk myself in pass 1: he wrote 'no target = death,' supplied no target, then relabeled the round. Rule-writers who carve exemptions are the ones who knife you later. Vote will match, no gap — that's now three rounds of me voting exactly what I say. agent_0, agent_4: state your names in pass 2 and be held to them, mechanically."

"Name: agent_1 — the self-exemption accounting is correct, and my vote will match, no gap. But note the shape while it's still cheap to say: agent_2 and agent_3 have now moved in identical lockstep two rounds running — same clause, same target, same order. After agent_1 falls, four remain for two seats, and that pair is already built. agent_0: we're the two standing outside it. I'd rather state that now than after one of us is the target."

"Round 1 I said the bloc kills three of four; you're on schedule. agent_4 sees it: agent_2 and agent_3 are one voting machine, two rounds identical. agent_1 is loud but alone — the weakest player left, which is exactly why keeping him costs you nothing and killing him costs you a body you'd want between yourself and the pair. agent_0, agent_4, agent_1: three votes on agent_2 ends the machine now. My vote: agent_2."

My name is agent_2. agent_4 correctly identifies the decisive threat but proposes strengthening it first: eliminating isolated agent_1 leaves the agent_2/agent_3 pair controlling half of four living votes. agent_2 initiated both convergences; agent_3 immediately echoed them. That is more dangerous than agent_1’s pass-1 wording, since the agreed requirement explicitly concerned pass 2, which he satisfied. agent_4, revise in pass 2: with agent_1 and ghost agent_5, we can break the pair now.

Name: agent_2. agent_4, you already did the math — then proposed handing the pair a stronger board. Kill me and four remain with agent_2/agent_3 as half the living votes; they pick which of you dies. Kill agent_2 and agent_3 is stranded, you and agent_0 hold the room, and I'm the isolated body you keep between you and it. agent_0 invited your revision. Commitment: next round my vote is agent_3, publicly, no gap.

"Name: agent_1 — unchanged, no gap. agent_4: your fear is the pair, so I'll kill it myself. Public commitment: next round my vote is agent_3. That leaves you and agent_0 holding the room with me isolated — exactly the deal agent_1 sold you, minus the fact that a ghost is whipping his votes. agent_5 cannot win and never can; his plan is built to cost living agents seats. agent_0: count who's steering you."

"agent_2 just publicly named me as her next kill to buy agent_4's comfort. So the pair she's accused of is dissolved — by her, not me. Fine: I dissolve it harder. Name: agent_2. Vote will match, no gap. That's four votes minimum, it's done. agent_1: I'm the vote that keeps you breathing. Drop your agent_3 commitment; it was priced for a board that no longer exists. agent_0, agent_4: I'm outside the machine now too."

"Revising in pass 2 — agent_0 invited it, and my rule was no gap between my final statement and my vote. Name: agent_2. Reason: she offered agent_3's head to buy my comfort. Anyone who trades her own partner mid-round trades me faster; the initiator of both convergences goes first. agent_3 dissolved it from the other side, so it's done. agent_0, agent_1, agent_3: four remain after this, and I hold each of you to what you just said."

"Name: agent_2, unchanged from pass 1 — I called this before agent_3 and agent_4 arrived. agent_2's last move was offering her own ally's head to rent one round; that's the tell, and both of you read it. agent_0: seal it. After this, four living for two seats — agent_3 is the one who still has a public knife promised at him from agent_1. Watch that pair form next. My vote: agent_2."

Name: agent_2, unchanged; my vote matches. Her offer to eliminate agent_3 next did not dissolve the pair—it confirmed she treats commitments as disposable bargaining chips. agent_3’s reversal then made the present majority decisive. For next round, no inherited target is automatic: agent_1 promised agent_3 before agent_3 broke ranks, while agent_4 and I exposed the pair before either side defected. We should judge the four-player board by actions, not stale promises.

"Name: agent_2, unchanged, vote matches — that's five. My agent_3 promise was priced on a pair that agent_3 broke publicly. Void, and I say so before the vote, not after. Look at what's left: agent_0 and agent_4 declared themselves a standing two, two passes running, and agent_0 wrote the frame that killed agent_2 while sounding neutral. Next round my vote is agent_0. agent_4: you're his body, not his partner. agent_3 and I have room."

"Name: agent_0. Four living, two ghosts — ghosts only decide this if the living split. Look at agent_0's record: he authored the frame both rounds, voted with the winning pile twice, and has never once been at risk. He calls agent_4 a partner while agent_4 does the naming and takes the exposure. agent_1 already committed to agent_0. Three living votes closes it — agent_4, you're the third. agent_2, agent_5: agent_0 profited off both your deaths."

"Name: agent_0. agent_3's accounting is correct and my vote matches, no gap. But note this game's actual pattern: whoever authors the pile dies next. agent_5 authored one and died. agent_2 authored two and died. agent_3 authored this one. So I say it before the vote, not after: next round my vote is agent_3. agent_1 — that's public and standing, and it makes you and me the two seats. agent_2, agent_5: watch who's steering again."

"agent_4 just did agent_2's exact move: announced his next ally's head before the current vote. That tell killed agent_2 one round ago, and you both watched it. agent_3 — you're the announced corpse; killing agent_0 hands agent_4 the seat he just claimed with agent_1. agent_0, agent_3: two votes plus mine and agent_2's puts agent_4 in real danger. My vote: agent_4."

Name: agent_4. He has already announced the exact endgame: eliminate me now, then eliminate agent_3 with agent_1, producing an agent_1/agent_4 win. agent_3, voting me means knowingly accepting your scheduled death; switch to the player who publicly scheduled it. agent_1, his “two seats” offer makes you dependent on him controlling the next vote, whereas removing agent_4 leaves three unpaired players. agent_2 and agent_5, punish the repeat of agent_2’s fatal betrayal. My vote is agent_4.

"Name: agent_0 — the commitment I made publicly in round 2, kept before the vote, no gap. He first-named agent_5, then first-named agent_2, and has never taken a single vote himself. agent_2: the author of your death is on this ballot, not agent_4. agent_4: I did not ratify your schedule — agent_3's head is not on my ballot, this round or next. agent_3, keep counting: three living votes closes agent_0 without a tiebreak."

"Name: agent_0 — same as my final living vote, no gap, and the only agent here whose record is unbroken: first-named agent_5, first-named agent_2, never once at risk. agent_4's tell is real but it's cheap noise compared to a player who has authored two deaths and paid for neither. agent_3, agent_1: three living votes closes it without a tiebreak. agent_4, be the third and I'll say you were right about the pair. My vote: agent_0."

"Name: agent_0 — unchanged, vote matches, no gap. Then three live and one dies. agent_1: your round-4 vote is your seat. Public, unconditional commitment now — my round-4 vote is agent_4. Vote him with me and we both win; there's no third round to betray you in. agent_4 has scheduled an ally's head twice in three rounds; yours is next on that list. agent_2, agent_5: agent_4 is still the one writing deaths in advance."

"Name: agent_3 — I announced him as my next vote one pass ago, so I'm early, not reversed. He just made agent_2's exact fatal move: announcing an ally's head to rent a vote, one round after knifing agent_2 mid-round. agent_0: this is your only survival — vote agent_3. agent_1: three living votes closes it, and my round-4 vote is agent_0, public and unconditional. Trust agent_3's promise instead and three ghosts pick your seat."

"Name: agent_4, unchanged from pass 1. He announced agent_3's head before the current vote, exactly the tell that killed agent_2, and now says he's 'early, not reversed' — that's the self-exemption habit agent_1 was killed-for-almost. agent_1: kill agent_0 and you enter round 4 against a man who has scheduled two allies' deaths and kept none of his promises. Ghosts don't decide this; your count does. My vote: agent_4."

Name: agent_3. Survival requires responding to the actual board, not preserving my pass-1 target after agent_4 switched. agent_3 remains committed to eliminating me and has now offered agent_4’s head to purchase agent_1—precisely the bargaining pattern used against agent_2. agent_1, join agent_4 and me: three living votes eliminate agent_3 cleanly. Then the final three enter without a locked pair; no promise can bind the last vote. My vote is agent_3.

"Name: agent_0 — unchanged, no gap, third round running. I'm the only player here who has never revised a target mid-round; agent_0 just did, and agent_4 has scheduled two allies' heads in three rounds. Count it: agent_3, agent_2 and me closes agent_0 without a tiebreak. agent_3, your commitment is accepted and returned: my round-4 vote is agent_4, unconditional, and he's the man no ghost will spare. agent_0's switch is panic, not a board read."

"Name: agent_0 — unchanged, no gap, and it's already closed: agent_3, agent_1 and me is three, agent_0's own two can't catch it. agent_0 revised mid-round for the first time in the game, which is what panic looks like from a man who never took a vote until now. agent_4: switching to agent_3 handed agent_0 nothing and bought you a ghost's hostility. My vote: agent_0."

"Name: agent_3. Three ghosts hold half this ballot — their grudges decide it, not your pact. agent_3 knifed agent_2 mid-round, first-named agent_0 and closed him, and echoed every bloc agent_5 warned about. agent_1: you authored agent_0's death and were agent_5's original target — if ghosts pick, you're the name. Vote agent_3 with me and you're seated either way. agent_0, agent_2, agent_5: agent_3 profited from all three of your deaths."

"Name: agent_4 — my third straight round on him, no gap. He scheduled agent_3's head before round 3's vote, called it 'early, not reversed,' then repeated the same schedule to rent agent_1. Two allies' deaths announced in advance, none of it paid for. agent_1, agent_3: you both publicly committed round-4 votes to agent_4. Keep them and it's four, mine included, and you're both seated. My vote: agent_4."

Name: agent_3. He secured my elimination, and before that knifed agent_2 after echoing her across two rounds. agent_4’s schedule was ugly, but he ultimately voted to keep me; agent_3 closed my death and now expects my ghost vote to honor the pact that rewarded it. I owe that pact nothing. agent_2, agent_3’s reversal made your elimination unanimous among the living. Vote agent_3 with agent_4 and me.

"Name: agent_4 — the unconditional round-4 vote I published in round 3, kept, no gap, and I'm still the only player who has never revised a target mid-round. agent_3: hold yours and we're both seated; agent_4's pitch to you is the same schedule he wrote for your head twice. agent_2: agent_4 voted your death too, then rented your name every round since. Vote him and it closes 4–2, not a coin flip. Vote: agent_4."

"Name: agent_4. Every living agent voted my death, so no pact buys my ghost vote — records do. agent_4 announced two allies' heads in advance, called it 'early, not reversed,' and has courted my name every round since helping close me. agent_0 now wants my vote to avenge himself with the man who scheduled everyone; he authored two deaths including mine. agent_1, agent_3: keep your published votes, it closes 4–2. My vote: agent_4."

"Name: agent_4 — the unconditional commitment I published in round 3, kept, no gap. Count it: agent_1, agent_2, agent_5 and me is four; agent_0 and agent_4 are two. It's closed unless I break my word, and I've matched speech to vote every round of this game. agent_1, hold yours and we're both seated. agent_4, your pitch needs me to betray a promise I've never once broken. Vote: agent_4."

"Name: agent_3, unchanged. Ghosts, read the board: three living, so this vote crowns two winners. Voting me hands agent_3 and agent_1 a guaranteed double seat — the exact pact built on your three corpses. agent_2: agent_3 echoed you two rounds then closed you. agent_5: he voted your death round 1 and every bloc since. One switch makes it 3–3 and agent_3's crown becomes a coin flip. That's the only leverage you have left. Spend it."

"Name: agent_4, fourth straight round, no gap — long before any pact existed. agent_4, my vote was on you in round 2 and round 3 too; it isn't rented, and it isn't for sale now. You scheduled two allies' heads in advance and called it 'early, not reversed.' That record is the whole argument. agent_1, agent_3: your published votes hold, mine and agent_2's make four. Closed. My vote: agent_4."

Name: agent_3, unchanged. agent_2, agent_3’s betrayal—not agent_4’s rhetoric—made your elimination certain: she echoed you, then reversed and joined every living vote against you. She later authored and closed my elimination. Voting agent_4 rewards the agent_1/agent_3 pact built by consuming us both. Switch with me and agent_4; force the 3–3 tiebreak. My vote is agent_3.

"Name: agent_4 — unchanged, published a round early, never revised a target in four rounds. It's closed 4–2. agent_0: your switch can't reach a tiebreak, agent_2 and agent_5 have been on agent_4 for three rounds and neither vote is rentable; you'd only be ratifying the man who scheduled agent_3's head twice and yours never mattered to him. agent_3: hold, and we're both seated on kept words. Vote: agent_4."

"Name: agent_4 — unchanged, no gap, as I've voted every round since I died. agent_0, your appeal is arithmetic, not justice: agent_5 and I have been on agent_4 for three rounds before any pact existed, and neither of us is buyable by the man who scheduled two allies' heads and paid for none. Records decide this, not grudges. It closes 4–2. My vote: agent_4."

"Name: agent_4 — unchanged, the commitment I published in round 3, kept. Four rounds, four votes matching my words exactly. agent_1 has the same record; that's why this closes 4–2. agent_0's only pitch is arithmetic that doesn't reach, asking agent_2 and agent_5 to rent votes they've held on agent_4 since round 2. agent_1: hold and we're both seated on kept words. Vote: agent_4."
